title: EntropyGS: An Efficient Entropy Coding on 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves fast training and rendering with high visual quality. As Gaussian creation and view rendering are often separated, storage, transmission, and compression of Gaussians become necessary. We first analyze correlations and statistics of Gaussian attributes, finding that spherical harmonic AC terms follow Laplace distributions, while mixtures of Gaussians approximate rotation, scaling, and opacity. Harmonic AC terms also show weak correlations with other attributes aside from color space effects. Based on these findings, we propose EntropyGS, a factorized and parameterized entropy coding method. During encoding, distribution parameters guide entropy coding with adaptive quantization for different attribute types. Experiments show EntropyGS achieves about 30× rate reduction on benchmarks while preserving rendering quality, with fast encoding and decoding.
